items.title: New York City in a blizzard
items.date: 1902 (catalogue: 'Probably photographed on February 17, 1902. Location: New York City.' Copyright: Thomas A. Edison; 24Feb1902; H14438)
items.depicts: Real Edison actuality of Madison Square, New York, during a blizzard; the camera slowly pans. Visible: men in long overcoats and bowler hats standing in thick falling snow beside a snow-covered streetcar; a horse-drawn fire engine trailing smoke; crowds around horse-drawn wagons and cabs; streetcars passing close to the lens; the snow-covered park with bare trees, an ornate lamp post and a monument; then the facade of a large hotel with huge snow banks and pedestrians trudging through deep snow. Black-and-white, soft, grainy paper-print image. No people posting letters, nothing Christmas-specific: use it as the 'winter city' atmosphere shot (it is New York 1902, not London 1843).
items.evidence: loc.gov catalogue summary: '"A realistic panoramic view taken at Madison Square, New York City, on February 17, 1902. A portion of the New York Fire Department is seen trying to make their way to a fire through the immense snow drifts. A few pedestrians are bravely plodding through the immense piles of snow, and a snow plow is hard at work on the Broadway, underground trolley line, endeavoring to clear the tracks. Madison Square, Madison Square Garden, Broadway, the Fifth Avenue Hotel, and 23rd Street are all shown in succession"--Edison films catalog.' Contributors: Thomas A. Edison, Inc; Paper Print Collection (Library of Congress). Genre: Actualities; Silent films; Nonfiction films. Downloaded file = the LoC National Screening Room mp4 linked from the item page (tile.loc.gov .../mbrs/ntscrm/01912444/01912444.mp4, 127,323,140 bytes, size matches the item record). items.title: Collecting mail, U.S.P.O.
items.date: 1903 (catalogue: 'Filmed August 10, 1903 in Washington, D.C.' Copyright: American Mutoscope & Biograph Company; 22Aug03; H34968. Cameraman A. E. Weed)
items.depicts: Real Biograph actuality, a sharp, steady close shot of two US mail boxes at a street corner: a small box marked 'U.S.M.' on a pole and a large round-topped box on legs marked 'U.S. MAIL'. A man in a dark suit and derby steps up and slips a letter into the small box (the white envelope is visible at ~18 s). A letter carrier with a shoulder satchel then unlocks the small box and empties the letters into his bag, then crouches at the large box to take out the mail. Behind them: a sunny, wide street with streetcars, cyclists, horse-drawn buggies, men in straw hats, women in long skirts and with a parasol. NOTE: this is SUMMER (August, bright sun, light clothing) in Washington D.C., not winter and not London; it shows the everyday ritual of posting and collecting letters.
items.evidence: loc.gov catalogue summary: '"The subject is the movement of mail by the U.S. postal service. As the film begins, two types of mail boxes on a pole on the corner of a street can be seen. In the background, away from the camera position, are people going by on foot, as well as horse-drawn and electric streetcar transportation. At the end of the film, a man wearing the uniform of a mailman is seen approaching the mail boxes. He unlocks the boxes and removes the mail from both the small and large boxes"--Early motion pictures.' Subjects: United States.--Post Office Department; Postal service--Washington (D.C.); Letter mail handling; Letter carriers. Biograph production no. 2467. The footage matches this description (the carrier appears at ~23 s rather than 'at the end'; his clothes do not read clearly as a uniform at this resolution). items.title: Sleighing in Central Park, New York
items.date: 1904 (catalogue: 'Photographed February 8, 1904 in Central Park, New York, N.Y.' Camera: Edwin S. Porter. Copyright: Thomas A. Edison; 4Mar1904; H43006)
items.depicts: Real Edison actuality: a snow-covered meadow/drive in Central Park with a dark band of bare and evergreen trees under a pale sky; one- and two-horse sleighs (including a pair with one white horse) glide across and come close past the camera, one wheeled carriage also passes; a long dark line of spectators/skaters stands along the far edge. Static camera, mostly wide. Black-and-white, fairly dark and contrasty, with flicker. Winter mood rather than street life; New York 1904, not London.
items.evidence: loc.gov catalogue summary: '"Showing a large number of people enjoying this favorite Winter pastime in Central Park. This scene was taken close by a large lake, and shows thousands of people skating in the background. A most interesting subject. 100 ft."--Edison films catalog no. 288.' Subjects: Sleighing--New York; Skating; Winter--New York (State)--New York; Central Park (New York, N.Y.). Contributors: Porter, Edwin S., camera; Thomas A. Edison, Inc; Paper Print Collection. (The skaters are only a dark line of figures in the distance in this transfer.) notes: All three are Library of Congress Paper Print Collection actualities (Edison 1902 and 1904, Biograph 1903) downloaded from tile.loc.gov as linked from each loc.gov item page, at the best mp4 offered (1440x1080 H.264, 4:3). Each mp4 is kept whole, so it still has the LoC logos and LoC-made title cards at the head and tail: use only the 'footage_span_s' part. There is no added music, narration or watermark inside the footage. None of the footage shows London or the 1840s, and none is a Christmas scene: it is US footage from about 60 years after 1843, so present it as period atmosphere (winter streets, posting letters), not as Cole's London. Rejected: 'Post man delivering mail, U.S.P.O.' (1903, https://www.loc.gov/item/00564566/). Its LoC video shows a postman climbing the steps of a stone townhouse, but the catalogue describes a rural two-horse 'U.S. Mail' wagon and a woman buying stamps, so the record and the footage disagree. I deleted that download. Not found at LoC for 1896-1910: a bare-footage London winter scene or a Christmas scene without intertitles.
